hed: Senate cloture on Clarity Act fails 49–50, short of 60 votes to open floor debate
dek: The Senate on Tuesday rejected cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, by a 49–50 tally — well short of the 60 votes required to end debate and take up the bill on the floor. The procedural loss is not a final-passage vote, but with fewer than 40 legislative days left before a new Congress and midterm campaigning underway, sponsors and industry advocates say the market-structure push is unlikely to revive before year-end. Negotiators had released a 635-page Sunday substitute said to incorporate 126 Democratic-requested edits, including Trump-accepted ethics limits and a Treasury stablecoin deposit-flight circuit breaker; Democrats sent an overnight counteroffer Monday that Republicans rejected before the vote. Multiple Republicans joined Democrats in voting no, so the motion did not even clear a simple majority.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: Cointelegraph’s post-vote wrap, Decrypt’s pre-floor ethics reporting, and American Banker’s stablecoin analysis cast the failure as ethics and banking safeguards still unresolved — highlighting Warren’s floor push to vote no over Trump-family crypto conflicts, Monday’s letter from 18 state attorneys general warning the bill could weaken state fraud enforcement, and bank-trade objections that the Treasury circuit breaker only triggers after deposit flight — while noting Bitcoin briefly slipped below $75,000 after the tally.

cr.body: CoinDesk’s floor-loss report, Decrypt’s quote of Lummis that a failed cloture means “we’re done” after 120-plus Democratic asks, and CoinGape’s write-through of Republicans rejecting the overnight counteroffer frame Tuesday as Democrats moving the goalposts and GOP holdouts joining them — with Lummis telling colleagues not to “hand our future to someone else,” industry PACs left to rethink midterm spending, and the SEC/CFTC now the default path for crypto rules without a market-structure statute.

stack_blurb: Senate Clarity Act cloture fails 49–50; short of 60; market-structure push stalled.
